content:
Hey, I wanted to try contributing to mathlib, so I tried writing up an IMO problem for the archive.

I think this is the official way to get feedback on it? If so, here is the link to the writeup

Would love any feedback

The problem is also proven at Compfiles - see https://live.lean-lang.org/#url=https%3A%2F%2Fdwrensha.github.io%2Fcompfiles%2Fproblems%2FCompfiles.Imo2000P2.sol.lean

Maybe this solution is useful for some inspiration or something. :)

Cheers
#mathlib4 > Feedback on first PR (IMO problem)

I see, I still would sort of like to learn about how to contribute to mathlib, and I figured this is a nice way to do so without modifying something too core

Is there some other way that I can help out?

I don't know in particular about the IMO portion of the mathlib and its policy, but the way I successfully started contributing is by upstreaming small useful lemmas (as in, <20 lines) that I developed in my personal projects
I think the IMO part might be the same. What is more valuable is the missing gap you find when formalizing a large solution. Filling those gaps are more important than the final result

Hmm ok, that seems like a plan, though I still feel a little uncertain.

For example, let us take theorem Nat.le_self_sq {n : ℕ} : n ≤ n^2, suppose I made such a theorem while working on one of my proofs, how would I then figure out

  1. Whether someone else has already added this, but it's not in the current version of mathlib
  2. Someone is 'assigned' to making it
  3. What file can I place it in
  4. How can I do so without creating merge conflicts with unrelated work on the same file
  5. Whether there is a more general way to write my theorem that I didn't think of because I am not aware of all of Mathlib (for example maybe my definition should work better with a typeclass that covers both Nat and Int or something)

What I figure I can do is use loogle to find out if such theorems exist, then search Zulip and Github PRs roughly for people talking about the same theorem.
Also, for 3. I am aware that #find_home is supposed to be used for this, but I am not sure I'm using it correctly.
For example, for this theorem it suggested [Mathlib.Tactic.Rify, Mathlib.Data.Nat.Factorial.BigOperators, Mathlib.Data.Nat.Fib.Basic, Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith.Frontend], none of these seem like the right place to me, my guess would be Mathlib.Data.Nat.Sqrt
I'm not sure what you mean in (1). That someone had added the lemma to mathlib and it has since been removed again?
Or do you mean something by "the current version of mathlib" that's different from what it seems to mean?
I just meant that someone has already created a PR that involves this theorem, but one that has not been merged into master yet

I question the underlying logic here. If you've just learnt python then your instinct shouldn't be "let's change some core python modules", it should surely be "let's make a new module". If you want to contribute to the lean ecosystem then why not do some maths in a new repo importing mathlib? Typically it is expert users, not beginners, who are actually changing mathlib itself.
